newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss stocks end little changed.
newsitem.headline: Swiss stocks end little changed.

text.p: Swiss shares ended Tuesday little changed with the blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) breaking off a four-day record run to end slightly below Monday's close.
The SMI's lower close, which followed a new all-time high at 4,734.1 points early in the day, showed how nervous the market was at the current levels, one Swiss dealer said.
Profit-taking and early Wall Street weakness took their toll on prices, although the all-share Swiss Performace (SPI) ended marginally higher.
The outlook remained favourable due to the lack of alternative investments, one trader said.

The SMI ended down 7.3 points, or 0.16 percent, at 4,677.1. The SPI was up 1.29 points, or 0.04 percent, at 2,9060.32. Volume was high with more than 3.3 billion francs' worth in shares traded on the bourse.

Attention concentrated on share rights in Ciba Specialty Chemicals. On their last day of trading, the rights ended two francs higher at 103.50 after falling earlier to 92.50 francs. On Monday night, a bank consortium said it would bid 90 francs per subscription right. Trade in shares in Ciba Specialty, which is being spun off from Novartis, will begin on Thursday.
Novartis registered shares slid 1.39 percent to 1,775. Roche was down 65 francs to 12,630.

Among financials, Union Bank of Switzerland bearers added seven francs to 1,355. Dealers said rumours that UBS held a nine percent stake in German DePfa-Bank had no impact on the price. UBS denied renewed claims by DePfa that UBS held a nine percent stake.
Credit Suisse Group jumped four francs to 170. SBC, which is to release its 1996 results on Wednesday, slid four francs to 303 due to profit taking.
Alusuisse and Sulzer posted gains of more than one percent. Second-tier Schindler registereds added 105 francs to 1,640 after releasing postitive results.
